**Y.G. Berger** (*International Statistical Review*, 2025; JCR Q1). [Read the article](https://doi.org/10.1111/insr.70001).

**The question.** How precise are the figures we get from large official surveys?

**What they found.**

- The margin of error can be computed without complex correction terms.
- The estimator is simple and asymptotically unbiased under stratified, multistage and informative designs.
- It also gives hypothesis tests and works under ordered systematic sampling.

**Key result (in the video).** A simpler way to get the margin of error. *Source: International Statistical Review (2025).*

**Why it matters.** Simple and reliable margins of error make it easier to use survey data correctly.

**Link with inequality.** Inequality and poverty are measured with complex surveys such as EU-SILC. Reliable margins of error tell us whether a change in inequality is real.
